title: Model ingress acceptance clauses and version safeguards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Clarify the acceptance criteria, manifest metadata, and runtime-safe versioning behavior for inbound open-model submissions (community weights and third-party builds). This PRD aims to remove ambiguity that causes production incidents when unvetted variants are routed to runtime infra: undefined tensor dtypes, incompatible attention kernels, and silent KV cache invalidation. The goal is a deterministic, minimal acceptance contract (manifest v2), a small heuristics-based runtime sanity probe, and explicit fallback semantics for unpinned or incompatible variants.
background: Over the last 9 months infra and support have responded to multiple incidents where community-submitted variants failed at runtime due to missing metadata (dtype, layer order), incompatible quantization metadata, or mismatched tokenizer specs. Current intake is inconsistent: some submissions rely on implicit defaults, others include partial manifests. This causes: increased onboarding time, runtime failures, and opaque rollback reasoning. We need a lightweight, enforceable admission contract that is actionable by infra, catalog, and runtime teams.
scope: In scope: manifest v2 schema requirements, minimum eval harness (3 prompt suites), runtime interop hash (deterministic ABI token), automated pre-ingress sanity probe, explicit pin/fallback operator semantics, error classification for onboarding failures, and required links to reproducible artifacts (weights storage, tokenizer, config). Out of scope: full Console UI for manifest editing (separate UX ticket), pricing/quoting changes for dedicated capacity.
requirements: 1) Submitter must provide manifest v2 with fields: architecture, dtype, layer_order, tokenizer_uri, weight_uri, recommended_quant_profile. 2) Model must pass three curated eval suites: safety/basic-hallucination, latency/throughput smoke, format/structured-output sanity. 3) Runtime interop hash must be computed by a canonical tool we provide and be included in manifest. 4) If model is unpinned, the catalog must attach a compatibility_hint entry with explicit incompatibilities (e.g., attention kernel mismatch). 5) Ingest pipeline must run a non-production sanity probe (<=30s) that validates forward pass on 1 batch; failures produce a triage label and block ingestion.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest v2 schema defined and documented in Confluence (fields, types, examples).
A canonical hashing tool and spec (runtime interop hash) checked into github.com/redwood-inference/model-tools with a CLI and versioned releases.
Ingestion pipeline updated to validate manifest v2 and run the 30s runtime sanity probe; failing manifests are rejected with deterministic error codes.

Acceptance errors map to three consumer-facing outcomes: Reject (fix required), Soft-allow with compatibility_hint (can be added to catalog as 'experimental - not pinned'), or Pin-required (cannot be routed without pin).
Engineers can reproduce failure locally using provided artifacts and a documented minimal repro flow.
Rollout policy: new experimental entries follow a canary rule (10% traffic, 24h minimum) before wider catalog exposure; policy encoded in catalog metadata.
design_feedback: Design reviewed: small manifest editor modal is preferred for quick fixes, but UI work is deferred. Design requested clearer user-facing language for compatibility_hint states; agreed to add 3 standard states: OK, WARNING, INCOMPATIBLE. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CAT/manifest-v2+UX
engineering_notes: Engineers raised two tradeoffs: 1) Strict byte-level ABI hash prevents benign rebuilds from entering catalog — proposed mitigation: include a build_metadata field and allow stable_semver aliasing. 2) Sanity probe runtime must run in isolated sandbox to avoid noisy noisy-profile interference; infra recommends ephemeral GPU sandbox VMs. ENG leads: schedule follow-up to scope cost impact (ENG-21800).
decisions: Adopt manifest v2 as minimum intake contract with a small required field set (architecture,dtype,tokenizer_uri,weight_uri).
Require runtime interop hash for all submissions; allow optional build_metadata to explain rebuild differences.
Support three catalog exposure states: pinned, experimental (soft-allow), blocked. Experimental entries must include compatibility_hint.

risks_mitigation: Risk: strict manifest enforcement could increase time-to-onboard for community contributors. Mitigation: provide a CLI 'manifest-fixer' to auto-populate defaults and a validation endpoint that returns line-by-line fixes. Risk: added sanity probe cost — mitigation: run probe on CPU quantized paths by default, escalate to GPU only for flagged architectures.
qa_plan: QA will use three representative community models (small/med/quantized) and run full ingest flow including manifest validation, runtime interop hash generation, and the 30s sanity probe. Expected pass: successful ingest for pinned and experimental entries for which compatibility_hint==OK. Repro steps in Confluence QA checklist.
